notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any state validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the stored result before validating payment state or amounts.
  Team convention requires every balance-changing operation to accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event>)` for a matching key and return the original result (including the stored record) without re-applying. Do this before state checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status has changed.
- [rb-0012] Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing a stub: Before writing a new function, read sibling modules (payments, audit, clock, money, errors) to reuse their helpers and error style.
  The accepted implementation reused `to_money`/`round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, `BillingError` from errors, and `audit.record` for the audit trail. Matching existing conventions (rounding, error codes, audit event naming) is what made the diff pass hidden tests.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0002] Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.
- [rb-0003] Read the existing test file before implementing: Locating and reading the relevant test file (tests/test_average_unit_price.py) alongside models.py and money.py clarified expected types and behavior before writing code.
  Before editing, cat the target module, its models, its money helpers, and any test file matching the feature name. This reveals signatures, Decimal usage, and edge cases, enabling a first-attempt pass.
- [rb-0004] Reject bool as int for integer validation: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bool when validating positive integers.
  When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

item.title: Honor team-convention review comments over literal issue signatures
item.description: When a review comment states a team convention (e.g., every money-moving operation must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None), apply it even if the issue text omits it.
item.content: Review comments labeled [team convention] are binding requirements, not distractors. Add the optional keyword-only parameter so existing callers still work, and implement the described behavior (check-first, return original result, include key in audit entry).

item.title: Check idempotency key before validating state
item.description: For idempotent operations, look up prior audit entries by key and return the original result before any state validation or mutation.
item.content: Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the stored record immediately. Only after that check should you validate payment.status and raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...). This prevents duplicate side effects and makes retries safe.

item.title: Follow sibling module conventions for state, time, and audit
item.description: Match existing patterns in the codebase (ensure_utc for timestamps, BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for wrong state, audit.record with event name and fields).
item.content: Before implementing, read sibling modules like invoice.py and payments.py to copy conventions: use ensure_utc(at) for stored times, raise BillingError('invalid_state', f'payment {payment.id} is {payment.status}') for invalid transitions, and call audit.record with a descriptive event name plus relevant fields including idempotency_key.
